ish: Add support for ISH chip This patch adds the initial support for ISH chip to enable the EC firmware to boot on Intel Integrated Sensor Hub (ISH). The following are enabled: 1. Inter-Processor Communication (IPC) driver that enables the ISH to communicate with the host Operating system via shared registers. 2. High Precision Event Timer (HPET) driver that provides configurable timers for the FW to use in task scheduling. 3. I2C bus driver for accessing sensors. 4. UART console driver with TX support only. [autotest] Increase MySQL connection timeout Increasing the connection timeout should make initial connection errors less likely. The default value seems to be 10 seconds (in MySQL documentation), but I think this depends on how the underlying MySQL C library was compiled. The logs in the bug suggest a timeout of ~5 seconds. Also, increase the overall timeout to 4 minutes to compensate for the increased per-try timeout. One concern is that if this is called in an RPC, the RPC response will timeout before this connection attempt. However, the existing 2 minute timeout already rules out this case. update chromeos-tpm-recovery to work for both TPM 1.x and 2.x This script runs when the target is booted in recovery mode. It reinitializes the TPM and sets the predefined NVRAM spaces to the default values. The precence of the /etc/init/trunksd.init file is used to derermine if the target is runnig TPM 1.x or 2.x. The major difference between TPM 1.2 and TPM 2.0 modes is that the TPM 2.0 supporting routines do not yet allow to define NVRAM spaces. This capability will be added later. BRANCH=none BUG=chrome-os-partner:59361, chrome-os-partner:55210 TEST=verified that running chromeos-TPM-recovery on a device booted in recovery mode properly reinitializes TPM on both reef (TPM2.0) and kevin (TPM1.2). The previously failing on reef autotest firmware_UpdateFirmwareDataKeyVersion is now passing. shill: cellular: improve service profile matching Like other technology types, shill uses the MAC address to derive a unique storage identifier for a cellular service based on the assumption that the MAC address of a cellular device (modem) is unique and remains constant across system reboots. Unfortunately, neither of these assumptions seems to be true for modems as a modem doesn't necesssarily have a MAC address or a valid one. Some modems may report the same MAC addresses while some don't report any. Also, a Linux kernel driver may pick a random MAC address for a modem when it fails to determine the MAC address. Due to these issues, shill may not reliably match a cellular service profile based on the storage identifier derived from MAC address, which leads to other side effects such as the user-provided APN not being persistently stored. This CL changes the cellular service profile to include other supposedly unique identifiers (IMSI, MEID) such that shill will use these identifiers to find a matching profile, regardless of the storage identifier. To maintain backward compatibility to an older profile, shill will fall back to the old way to locate a profile based on storage identifier when the new approach fails to find a matching profile. BUG=chromium:457364 TEST=Tested the following: - New unit tests pass. - Manually verify that shill finds an older service profile based on the storage identifier that matches the MAC address of a modem. - Using a modem that is assigned a random MAC address by the kernel driver, manually verify that shill finds a matching service profile based on other service properties even when the storage identifier doesn't match the MAC address. Change-Id: I9a13201789cf15eec64feb65d559429708cbd564 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/404633 Commit-Ready: Ben Chan <benchan@chromium.org> Tested-by: Ben Chan <benchan@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Prathmesh Prabhu <pprabhu@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Vincent Palatin <vpalatin@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: tpm: cr50: Don't use interruptible sleep If we are waiting for the TPM to be ready and userspace is frozen (for going to suspend) then the wait may get interrupted and the userland process using /dev/tpm0 will receive a ERESTARTSYS error code. However since this has now interrupted a transaction the TPM state machine will be out of sync and it will not respond properly so userland can't actually do anything for this error code. If we make the delay not interruptible then this particular type of failure does not happen. There are still possible places where the overall transaction could get interrupted and therefore out of sync, but this is the common case that is easy to reproduce. BUG=chrome-os-partner:59191 TEST=manual testing on eve board: ( while true ; do tpm_manager_client status >/dev/null; done ) & echo 1 > /sys/module/suspend/parameters/pm_test_delay echo freezer > /sys/power/pm_test while true ; do echo mem > /sys/power/state ; done Change-Id: I7cb8c15fb71d0e40b59150ef54f32d489c64e46c Signed-off-by: Duncan Laurie <dlaurie@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/407798 Commit-Ready: Duncan Laurie <dlaurie@google.com> Tested-by: Duncan Laurie <dlaurie@google.com> Reviewed-by: Aaron Durbin <adurbin@chromium.org>

Cr50: I2CS TPM: Ensure HW read fifo is empty for register reads This change is a safegaurd to ensure that TPM register data is always placed in the correct location in the HW read I2CS fifo. It is only checked for 1 or 4 byte regsiter reads. Because of the way in which a TPM command is sent and the response is read, there are multiple reads of the STS register prior to reading the TPM fifo register. Therefore ensuring the fifo has zero depth when 1 or 4 byte regsiter reads, improves the robustness of the design. Added a counter to track the number of times the fifo is adjusted and a new console command 'i2cs disp|rst' to display the count and reset it to 0 if desired. Removed section in code for TPM fifo register reads intended to handle the case where there was a mismatch between how many bytes were copied into the fifo and the number read by the host. Since the burstcount field in the status register always contains a valid amount of data that can be read by the host, there should not be cases where the host reads less data than was copied from the TPM fifo register. In the unexpected cases where the host may not drain all of the I2CS read fifo data during a TPM register read, the I2CS fifo depth will be corrected the next time that it reads either the access or STS register which happens prior to the start of any TPM transaction. BRANCH=none BUG=chrome-os-partner:57338,chrome-os-partner:59191 TEST=manual Booted Reef and verfied that TPM functionality is working. laptop-mode-tools: Refactor usb_autosuspend::listed_by_id usb_autosuspend's listed_by_id functions is horribly inefficient, it launches dozens of child processes for each USB device. vboot2: Allocate more buffer for kernel verification The low-level verification functions' *_WORKBUF_BYTES constants assume the work buffer is already aligned to VB2_WORKBUF_ALIGN. But malloc() may return a less-aligned pointer, in which case vb2_workbuf_init() aligns it (and loses a bit of space in the process). This can cause an error "vb2_rsa_verify_digest: ERROR - vboot2 work buffer too small!". High-level functions should be using the *_WORKBUF_RECOMMENDED_SIZE constants for allocation, which have enough padding to compensate for alignment problems. host_command_pd: reduce to 5msec delay in between PD interrupt handling Since PD task are highest priority, the 50msec delay between was intended allow other tasks to execute if PD has continuous interrupt. With two separate TCPC handled by host_command_pd task, interrupt from one TCPC will block the interrupt handling of another TCPC by this 50msec and cause error in the PD negotiation. Reduced to 5msec to ensure TCPC interrupt is handled as soon as possible while allow other tasks to execute if needed.
